learning_outcomes.text: Uses descriptive techniques to summarize, classify, and present data.
Is able to apply the fundamental concepts, applications, and results of probability.
Understands the basic concepts of random variables and identifies the most important discrete and continuous distributions.
Knows the main point estimators and confidence intervals.
Correctly formulates statistical hypotheses and selects the appropriate procedure for their acceptance or rejection.
Performs descriptive data analysis and solves problems of probability calculation, estimation, and hypothesis testing using computer software.
Identifies and formulates linear programming problems.

syllabus_topics: Random Variables. Main Discrete and Continuous Distributions
Introduction to spreadsheet application, LibreOffice Calc.
assessment_rules: The preferred assessment method is continuous evaluation, consisting of short answer tests (50%) and an exam (50%). Short answer tests include lab practicals (30%), assessed via questionnaires, and two short answer questionnaires (20%). A minimum score of 5 out of 10 must be obtained on the exam for continuous evaluation grades to be summed. Continuous evaluation is failed if the student does not attend the May exam or the total score is less than 5 out of 10. For the second and subsequent calls, the course will be evaluated solely by a single assessment exam, which requires a minimum score of 5 out of 10 to pass. Students must communicate their choice for single assessment via the virtual classroom before the end of the semester, unless they have submitted at least 40% of the continuous evaluation tests.
